incident.headline: The peninsula remains evacuated; the Lège-Cap-Ferret mayor says the fire is still at the commune gates and not mastered.
incident.summary: The latest reviewed local signal is TVCapFerret’s 19:30 CEST summary of Mayor Philippe de Gonneville’s update: the fire remains at the gates of Lège-Cap-Ferret and is still not mastered, firebreaks around Claouey, Lège and La Pignada have been built or reinforced, patrols and home/animal checks continue, and 700-800 firefighters are being hosted in Lège as a logistics point. The broader official baseline remains the Gironde prefecture’s 13:00 point: 42,000 hectares burned, nearly 220,000 people preventively evacuated in 23 communes, 75 firefighters treated, 240 homes destroyed, major road closures including parts of the A63, and 2,500 firefighters with 18 aircraft plus military and police support. Cap Ferret remains evacuated and no-return/no-tourist-access advice is unchanged. Bordeaux Airport still lists arrivals and departures; terminal operation, overnight hotel-zone evacuation and tram-stop disruption remain separate from flight operation.

materialUpdates.detail: Reuters reports that the uncontrolled Gironde fire changed orientation late Friday after a wind reversal and began progressing east toward the Bordeaux metropolitan area. The interior minister described the phenomenon as unprecedented and reported about 14,000 hectares burned and more than 110,000 Gironde evacuations. Franceinfo reports preparations for three additional metropolitan evacuations, says residents of Saint-Médard-en-Jalles and Saint-Jean-d’Illac should be ready for a probable evacuation, and records severe outbound congestion at Andernos. A later media report places the affected area near 19,000 hectares; that higher figure awaits matching official confirmation.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: This is a new trajectory and evacuation phase: the fire is no longer advancing only around the northern Bassin and peninsula corridor but has turned east toward metropolitan Bordeaux. The strongest late totals rise from 12,500 to about 14,000 hectares and from 44,000 to more than 110,000 Gironde evacuations, with a later media estimate near 19,000 hectares.

sources.name: Franceinfo live coverage supplied by the reader
Reuters reporting the wind reversal and eastward progression
Libération live coverage supplied by the reader

materialUpdates.title: Arcachon Bay partly reopens, but Cap Ferret maritime access remains restricted
materialUpdates.detail: The maritime prefecture’s order 2026-132 adapts the earlier Arcachon Bay navigation ban: zones farthest from the fire can reopen to sea users, while the west side of the bay and 0.25-nautical-mile safety circles around the evacuation embarkation points remain closed. UBA evacuation boats have been suspended by decision of the Gironde prefect.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: This is a maritime-access improvement for parts of Arcachon Bay, not a reopening of Cap Ferret. It removes the blanket bay-closure signal but keeps ordinary passenger ferries, leisure boating near the peninsula, and public maritime access to the evacuated peninsula unavailable.

sources.name: Atlantic maritime prefecture partial-reopening notice, 24 July
Maritime prefecture order 2026-132, created 18:26 CEST

materialUpdates.title: Reuters attributes 12,500 hectares and 44,000 evacuations to the prefecture’s 14:00 briefing
materialUpdates.detail: Reuters’ later version says the Gironde prefecture’s 14:00 situation update put the still-uncontrolled Saumos fire at more than 12,500 hectares. It reports 44,000 evacuations over 48 hours, alongside about 1,000 firefighters, more than 260 ground vehicles, 53 homes and one campsite destroyed; it also lists Arès and Andernos for preventive evacuation. The evacuation and Arcachon Bay navigation restrictions remain operative; this confirmation does not establish a reopening.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The higher 12,500-hectare and 44,000-evacuation totals are now attributed by Reuters to the prefecture’s 14:00 briefing, rather than standing only as a local-media report. Its later version also adds Andernos to the reported preventive-evacuation scope. No access or reopening change follows.

sources.name: Reuters reporting the Gironde prefecture’s 14:00 situation briefing
Mairie de Lège-Cap-Ferret incident notice (evacuation remains the operative authority instruction)

materialUpdates.title: Midday briefing confirms a larger response, firefighter injuries and extensive property loss
materialUpdates.detail: The latest prefectural and emergency-service briefing puts about 1,000 firefighters on the Gironde fire. Authorities report 53 homes and one campsite destroyed, 2,000 homes saved, and 27 firefighters treated, including six taken to hospital; no deaths have been reported. The SDIS says the fire advanced at 800–1,000 hectares per hour for several hours overnight, while forecast westerly gusts of up to 80 km/h remain a concern.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The response has risen from about 800 to about 1,000 firefighters. The clearest official damage and injury assessment is now 53 homes and one campsite destroyed, 27 firefighters treated and six hospitalised, with no deaths reported.

sources.name: AFP reporting the midday prefectural and SDIS briefing
Reuters reporting the midday briefing

materialUpdates.title: Evacuation expands to Arès and ordinary navigation is prohibited on Arcachon Bay
materialUpdates.detail: Reuters reports that the prefecture ordered a mandatory preventive evacuation in Arès and that the maritime prefecture imposed a temporary navigation ban on Arcachon Bay. The restriction confirms that a listed ferry timetable cannot be treated as an available public route to Cap Ferret.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The disruption has expanded beyond the peninsula: Arès is under mandatory evacuation and ordinary navigation on the bay is temporarily prohibited.

sources.name: Reuters reporting the prefectural and maritime measures

materialUpdates.title: Interior Minister reports more than 10,000 hectares burned and about 40,000 evacuations
materialUpdates.detail: At Friday morning's national briefing, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the Saumos fire had passed 10,000 hectares and led to about 40,000 evacuations; he also said it was not under control and was continuing to progress. AFP later reported 80 homes burned, including about 50 destroyed, so the dashboard does not treat all 80 as confirmed total losses. This is a later, materially higher assessment than overnight prefecture-based reporting.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The best later public briefing raises the reported footprint above 10,000 hectares and puts evacuations at about 40,000; the fire was still progressing and not controlled. Later reporting distinguishes 80 homes burned or affected from about 50 destroyed.

sources.name: Public Sénat reporting the Interior Minister briefing
Le Monde live reporting
AFP reporting the later property-loss clarification

materialUpdates.title: The affected area has nearly doubled and the fire remains uncontrolled
materialUpdates.detail: Late Thursday the prefecture reported about 4,800 hectares affected. Friday-morning reporting based on the latest authority briefings moved first to 8,700 hectares and then towards 10,000 hectares. Civil Protection described the Saumos fire as the largest of the season and said it was not under control.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: The reported footprint moved from about 4,800 hectares to at least 8,700 and potentially 10,000; authorities still did not describe the fire as controlled.

sources.name: Feux de Forêt
Civil Protection reporting

materialUpdates.title: Evacuation extended to the entire Cap Ferret peninsula
materialUpdates.detail: The prefecture ordered the third and final evacuation phase, requiring everyone still present from Claouey to the tip of Cap Ferret to leave. The RD106 was designated as the road exit towards Bordeaux, with temporary maritime evacuation shuttles from Grand Piquey, Le Canon, Port de la Vigne and Bélisaire.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: Le Canon moved from a threatened location to an explicit evacuation zone, and maritime shuttles were added to the road evacuation.

sources.name: Gironde Prefecture reporting
Feux de Forêt

materialUpdates.title: The fire breached a defensive containment line
materialUpdates.detail: The prefecture said the fire crossed a line established by firefighters at around 01:00. That breach triggered the rapid expansion of evacuation orders down the peninsula.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: A firefighting line failed at about 01:00, directly triggering the rapid extension of evacuation orders down the peninsula.

sources.name: Le Monde live reporting

access.name: Travel to the peninsula
access.detail: The entire peninsula remains under an evacuation order. Public inbound travel is not permitted; Lège-Cap-Ferret town hall still says not to return, road access is closed and the partial Arcachon Bay reopening does not create a public maritime route to Cap Ferret.

access.name: Road access · Claouey

access.name: Road access · Petit Piquey & Piraillan

access.name: Road access · Le Canon & L’Herbe

access.name: Road access · Cap Ferret
access.detail: No authority has announced that ordinary inbound road access to Cap Ferret village or Bélisaire has reopened. The evacuation order and peninsula access restrictions still apply.

access.name: Maritime leisure activities
access.detail: Some Arcachon Bay zones far from the fire have reopened, but the peninsula remains evacuated and the maritime-prefecture order keeps the west-coast corridor and embarkation-point safety zones closed.

access.name: Beaches
access.detail: Residents and visitors have been told to leave the area. Municipal lifeguard stations are closed.

access.name: Cycling & hiking
access.detail: All forest cycle paths are closed; Gironde remains at red-level wildfire risk.

localCommerce.name: Groceries and food shops
localCommerce.detail: The evacuation order prevents normal customer access. No general reopening of supermarkets, food shops or the Cap Ferret market has been announced.

localCommerce.name: Pharmacies
localCommerce.detail: No pharmacy-specific reopening or public-access arrangement has been found. Emergency and authority instructions take priority over normal listed hours.

localCommerce.name: Other local shops and services
localCommerce.detail: There is no general announcement that visitor-facing retail or everyday local services have resumed.

ferries.name: Arcachon ↔ Bélisaire ferry
ferries.detail: Arcachon Bay has partly reopened away from the fire, but the west side of the bay and safety circles around Bélisaire, La Vigne, Le Canon, Grand Piquey and Piquey remain restricted. The UBA timetable is not an available public route to the evacuated peninsula.

ferries.name: Emergency evacuation shuttles
ferries.detail: The maritime-prefecture notice says the Union des Bateliers Arcachonnais evacuation boats have been suspended by decision of the Gironde prefect, while embarkation zones are preserved in case maritime evacuation resumes.

ferries.name: Excursions and leisure boats
ferries.status: Partly reopened away from the fire
ferries.detail: Sea users may return only to zones farthest from the fire. Navigation remains prohibited along the west-coast corridor of Arcachon Bay and within safety circles around the evacuation embarkation points.

overall.sourceName: Bordeaux Airport board updated at 00:01 CEST; prefectural evacuation notices

closure.status: Elevated risk · flights operating but heavily disrupted
closure.detail: The official board still lists arrivals and departures, but it flags 2 delayed and 2 cancelled arrivals, plus 0 delayed and 0 cancelled departures. The airport's own flash notice says activity continues, while the hotel zone around the airport is evacuated until further notice and the halls close overnight, so the site cannot provide accommodation. Treat flight operation, terminal overnight access and ground access as separate signals.

groundAccess.status: Disrupted · hotel zone evacuated and airport tram stops skipped
groundAccess.detail: Bordeaux Airport says activity continues and bus/tram services remain provided, but the tram is not stopping between Merignac Soleil and the airport. A separate airport flash notice says the surrounding hotel zone is evacuated by prefectural decision until further notice; because Hall A, Hall B and terminal billi are closed overnight, no accommodation can be provided on the airport site. Travellers are directed to hotels outside evacuated zones or the Parc des Expositions.
